body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The big local story today is a judge's order that Kern County redo the environmental review of CRC's Carbon TerraVault 1 carbon-capture project — a ruling that lands squarely in the middle of the valley's energy future. Outside, expect a mild November day, a high near 74 and a low around 52 tonight, with no active weather alerts and air quality sitting at a moderate 86. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most notable stop came just after 4 a.m., when officers pulled over a vehicle that dispatch had linked to an earlier weapons case. Domestic violence calls carried most of the rest of the evening. Officers were sent at 7:41 p.m. to the 2,100 block of Kentucky Street in east Bakersfield, where a man fled inside the home; a records check turned up a domestic violence restraining order already on file, and he was arrested on suspicion of domestic battery and resisting.

Deputies were sent at 10:58 p.m. to a domestic disturbance on Big Blue Road, where a man was reported to have threatened to kill a woman. Officers answered a domestic call at an apartment on the 1,300 block of Oregon Street in east Bakersfield at 10:12 p.m., where the person reported was under the influence. And on a domestic battery call at 11:56 p.m., a woman told officers her boyfriend had battered her.

Fire crews were sent at 8:29 p.m. to an apartment fire on the 700 block of L Street in central Bakersfield, where the unit was burning. The building was evacuated and crews checked the attic for extension before the assignment was downgraded about twenty minutes later. Crews were sent back to the same block shortly before 2 a.m. for a fire call at an apartment.

Elsewhere, a pursuit ran eastbound on Highway 58 at 10:39 p.m. at speeds reported near 90 mph and climbing. And at 4:48 a.m., a small pickup and a semi-trailer collided in the Love's Travel Stop lot on Taft Highway, leaving one patient with a traumatic injury.

## Today's weather

It's currently 54 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 74 this afternoon and a low around 52 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality is 86, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to particulates, it's a reasonable day to keep an eye on how you're feeling during longer stretches outdoors. Otherwise, this is about as easy a November Tuesday as the valley gives us: light layers in the morning, short sleeves by mid-afternoon.

## Top stories

**A Kern County judge has ordered the county to redo the environmental review of California Resources Corporation's Carbon TerraVault 1 project, 23ABC reports.** Judge Marcos Camacho ruled the project's environmental impact report falls short, finding it didn't fully address where the carbon dioxide would come from, the potential for leaks, and how much carbon the project would actually capture. The lawsuit was filed against the county by environmental groups challenging its review, not against CRC directly. CRC CEO Francisco Leon called the order "a step in the wrong direction" and said it reflects what he described as the weaponization of CEQA by a narrow group of special interests. Cesar Aguirre of the Central California Environmental Justice Network told 23ABC the ruling is a step toward transparency, saying the county has to come back to the table and make sure the community is part of the decision-making. Why it matters here: Carbon TerraVault 1 is central to Kern's pitch as a carbon-capture hub, and this ruling could slow permitting and injection work at a moment when the county's energy economy is already in transition.

**Bakersfield's police chief says keeping officers is now harder than filling the ranks ever was, according to 23ABC.** Chief Brent Stratton told the station that officers are leaving faster than usual, many for other law enforcement agencies. "Normally we're adding 50 or so and losing about 25, so I'm gaining about 25 a year. This year, losing 50," Stratton said. BPD briefly reached full staffing earlier this year by hiring ahead of expected losses, but Stratton described a statewide supply-and-demand problem — too few officers, too much demand — that leaves experienced ones free to choose. That competition is playing out across the county: Shafter Police Chief Randy Milligan said more BPD officers are applying to his department than in years past, reversing a trend that once ran the other way, and Shafter is now fully staffed with about ten people waiting for an opening. Delano hired four laterals from neighboring agencies this past year, including one from BPD, and is offering a $15,000 hiring bonus, a three-12 schedule and added incentive pay. For residents, the practical question is what staffing churn means for response times and neighborhood coverage.

**A pregnant former foster youth is fighting to avoid homelessness again, 23ABC reports.** Leslie Olivarez, 31 and eight months pregnant, experienced homelessness as a foster youth and is now trying to keep from returning to it before her December due date. She told the station she aged out of foster youth benefits at 21 and has struggled to find resources since; her grandparents, long her fallback, have been evicted. She said she waited eight years for her Section 8 application to be processed, was finally approved, and then hit more delays in actually using the benefits. Janessa Fisher, a former foster youth who now works for the Dream Center, said 30 to 40 percent of foster youth experience homelessness, and pointed to Homeless Youth Awareness Month as a reminder that the goal is to reach young people before they age out. It's a story that puts a face on a housing pipeline problem Kern County sees every year.

**KGET 17 is tracking the money behind this year's Congressional District 22 race, breaking down what it cost candidates to win — and to lose.** The station's campaign-cash analysis looks at the fundraising and spending totals on both sides of a contest that drew heavy outside attention to the southern San Joaquin Valley. We'll have the full breakdown as the numbers settle.

**Also from KGET 17: the area around a hit-and-run that killed a 12-year-old has a history of pedestrian deaths.** The station reports the stretch has seen repeated collisions involving people on foot, a pattern that raises familiar questions about lighting, crosswalks and speed along a corridor residents already know as dangerous.

**And in sports, KGET 17 reports the 2026 CIF Central Section football playoffs have Bakersfield schools in the top divisions reaching the semifinal round.** Postseason football is down to the wire, with local programs still alive in the bracket's biggest tiers.

## Something good

There's a genuine bright spot in that playoff news: Bakersfield schools will feature in the top divisions of the 2026 CIF Central Section football playoffs, with local teams advancing to the semifinal round. It's a proud stretch for the players, the coaches and the families who have been in the stands all fall, and a reminder that the valley's Friday night lights still produce some of the best football in the section. If you've got a team still playing, this is the week to show up.

## Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full calendar ahead. NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet takes the stage Friday, November 13 — an early start to the holiday season downtown and a good one for families. Then on Sunday, November 15, the Fox hosts the 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards, a hometown celebration of the sound this city is known for around the world. Looking further out, the Fox has Cults & Classics: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? on November 23, Becky Robinson's Holiday Spectacular on November 27, and the Shrek Rave — Shrek The Halls — on December 4, with a Cults & Classics season pass covering the 2026–2027 series.

No public meetings are listed on the county or city calendars for today, so it's a quiet one on the civic front. That won't last: with the Carbon TerraVault ruling now in hand, expect the county's environmental review process — and the public comment that comes with it — to move back onto the agenda in the weeks ahead. We'll flag those dates as soon as they're posted.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield. Drive carefully on the morning commute, and we'll see you tomorrow.

top.title: Judge orders Kern County to redo environmental review of CRC's Carbon TerraVault 1 project
